fields.why: No health coverage and inability to see a doctor because of cost are analyzed as outcomes; the brief counts determinants analyzed as the outcome (its example: problems paying medical bills). Medicaid expansion alone would not count (overall trend).

Table 1 gives a per-level p-value (each level vs the rest, logistic model with caregiving status as outcome) for 7 age, 8 race/ethnicity and several SES groups; rule 2's symmetric Table-1 case applies, so this is not mere composition.
Age (7 levels), race/ethnicity (8), and SES via education (4), employment (7), income (7) and home ownership (3); sex has only 2 levels.
Each demographic indicator is tested against the rest (V6a: each level vs the rest is per-group vs referent only); no omnibus or joint test is reported.

brief_issues: Rule 6 (composition is not groupwise) and rule 2 (symmetric Table-1 tests count the SPD margin) pull apart when a Table 1 gives per-level tests of composition between two non-SPD groups; the brief could state that rule 2 governs whenever a test is reported per SPD level.
